key_insight: As Reynolds number increases, submerged oil-jet breakup shifts from Rayleigh–Plateau instability to shear-driven breakup, while droplet coalescence helps shape the resulting size distribution.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for both breakup and coalescence can improve droplet-size predictions for oil-spill response and liquid–liquid extraction.
method: Simultaneous PIV and PLIF measurements of silicone oil injected into refractive-index-matched sugar water.
POD identifies interfacial instability modes; CNN-based segmentation extracts droplet sizes.
Population balance models are extended to include droplet coalescence.
evidence_signal: Experiments show transitional bimodal droplet sizes evolving toward a smaller, single-mode distribution at higher Reynolds numbers, with coalescence improving model agreement especially for larger droplets.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the tested liquid pair requires validation; the abstract provides no quantitative prediction errors or segmentation accuracy.
paper_title: Submerged Immiscible Oil Jet: Breakup Dynamics and Droplet Size Modelling
